prompt.context: It's Monday morning and as a new Principal/Engagement Manager, you've just gotten a call from a well known and respected French-based Consumer Products company. The company has offices in the US and has been selling through traditional channels throughout its history. It designs and manufactures plastic products like pens, pencils, disposable razors, etc. It's an old company that's been around for about 60 years and wants to take advantage of the Internet, starting with US sales. You talked at length with the President of the dot-com part of the company and learned: the company wants to sell directly to consumers through their Internet site; their current online business is a small catalog not doing well (sales and hits less than expected); it offers convenience (open 24x7, more product info) but limited selection (only high-margin items); the President wants to add three specific functionalities: (1) multi-ship-to functionality, (2) site-wide search functionality, and (3) checkout sales / impulse buy items similar to end caps in grocery stores; and she wants your consulting team to build this immediately. This coming Thursday, you will meet with the President and her team. Her expectation is that you will present a plan for your consulting team to build the functionality ASAP.
prompt.question: What will you do on Monday? What will you prepare? What questions will you ask the President? What is your goal for that meeting?

clarifying_info.q: Who is the target customer for the online store?
clarifying_info.a: The President has not clearly defined this yet — it is one of the open questions to explore.

clarifying_info.q: What does success look like for the online business in terms of metrics?
clarifying_info.a: The President is focused on increasing hit rate and improving revenue, but specific targets have not been set.

clarifying_info.q: Why are current sales and hits below expectations?
clarifying_info.a: Root cause is not yet known; that is part of what needs to be investigated.

clarifying_info.q: What is the budget or timeline for building the new functionality?
clarifying_info.a: She wants it built immediately, but specifics have not been discussed.

framework: Clarify the real business problem: the client is asking for a solution (build features), but the underlying problem (low traffic and revenue) may not be solved by those features — challenge the premise before accepting the build scope
Diagnose why the current online business underperforms: examine value proposition (convenience vs. price vs. selection), target customer definition, and channel fit
Assess the proposed functionalities against the diagnosed problem: do multi-ship-to, site-wide search, and checkout upsells actually address the root cause of low hits and sales?
Define the goal for Thursday's meeting: frame it as an information-gathering and alignment session, not a build-plan presentation
Prepare a structured line of questioning for the President covering: target customer, value proposition, competitive differentiation, and how the online store will deliver on its promise
Recommend a discovery/diagnostic phase before committing to build, with clear success metrics defined upfront

questions.prompt: What should you do on Monday to prepare for Thursday's meeting?
questions.guidance: A strong answer avoids accepting the client's request at face value. The candidate should plan to: (1) research the company and its online business; (2) develop hypotheses about why the online store is underperforming; (3) draft a structured set of questions to challenge the President's proposed solution and uncover the true problem; (4) prepare a framework for diagnosing the online business rather than a build plan.

questions.prompt: What is your goal for the Thursday meeting?
questions.guidance: The goal should NOT be to present a build plan. The candidate should articulate that the goal is to open a conversation with the President and her team to better understand the online business's true issues and goals. Specifically: gather information to diagnose root causes of low traffic and sales, test whether the proposed functionalities actually address those root causes, and align on a diagnostic or discovery phase before committing to development work.

questions.prompt: What questions will you ask the President?
questions.guidance: The candidate's questioning should follow a logic path around the online store's value proposition. Strong questions include: Who is the store trying to target (target customer segment)? What is the store's real value to the customer — convenience, price, or selection? Why is the offering unique and attractive versus competitors or other channels? How will the online store deliver on that promise? Why are current hits and sales below expectations — has any analysis been done? What would success look like in 12 months? The candidate should avoid jumping straight to 'here is the build plan' and instead demonstrate hypothesis-driven consulting thinking.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the possible root causes for the online store's underperformance (low hits and low sales)?

categories.name: Value Proposition / Offering
ideas: Limited selection (only high-margin items) may not attract enough customers
Products (pens, razors, pencils) are low-involvement commodities — customers may not seek them out online
Pricing may not be competitive versus mass retail or Amazon
Convenience benefit (24x7, product info) may not be meaningful enough to drive traffic

categories.name: Target Customer & Awareness
ideas: Target customer not clearly defined, leading to unfocused marketing
Low brand awareness online in the US market
No SEO or digital marketing strategy driving traffic
Customers unaware the brand sells direct-to-consumer

categories.name: User Experience & Site Quality
ideas: Poor site navigation or search (which is why site-wide search is being requested)

categories.name: Channel Conflict
ideas: Existing retail partners may be unhappy with direct-to-consumer competition
Price parity issues between online and retail channels
Company culture or capabilities not built for e-commerce

categories.name: Operational / Fulfillment
ideas: Shipping costs make small-ticket commodity items uneconomical to buy online
No multi-ship-to capability limits gifting use cases

recommendation: Do NOT present a build plan on Thursday; instead frame the meeting as a structured diagnostic session
Before committing to any development work, conduct a 2–3 week discovery phase to define the target customer, clarify the value proposition, and identify root causes of underperformance

The three proposed functionalities (multi-ship-to, site-wide search, checkout upsells) may have merit but should only be prioritized after the root cause analysis confirms they will move the needle on hits and revenue
risks: The President expects a build plan and may push back on a discovery-first approach — manage expectations diplomatically
Delay in building functionality could erode the President's confidence in the consulting team
The online business may have structural issues (commodity products, channel conflict) that no feature additions can fix
next_steps: Monday: research company, draft diagnostic framework, prepare structured question list for Thursday
Tuesday–Wednesday: align internally with team on hypotheses and interview approach
Thursday meeting: present a brief summary of what you've learned, explain the discovery-first rationale, and walk through the diagnostic questions to open the President's eyes to the broader problem
Post-Thursday: propose a short discovery workplan with clear deliverables and timeline before any build commitment
